result.title: Visual Harness Scales General VLMs to Medical Images
result.summary: We show that an appropriate visual harness can substantially improve the performance of general vision-language models (VLMs) across diverse medical imaging tasks. We introduce VERA, a medical visual harness that equips general VLMs with interactive visual tools and systematic diagnostic evidence management. With VERA, general VLMs interactively explore medical images and progressively acquire diagnostic evidence, which is preserved in a lossless memory for subsequent retrieval and use. After submitting an initial answer, the VLM receives an assessment of potential omissions and the reliability of identified findings. This assessment guides further image inspection and measurement, followed by answer revision in an iterative agentic loop until sufficient evidence is obtained. Across 11 tasks and four imaging modalities, VERA improves performance on all tasks with Qwen3.8-27B, with notable gains in spleen measurement (63.3% to 98.3%), renal search (57.5% to 71.2%), and pulmonary nodule detection (0.0% to 28.2%). High-capability API-based VLMs achieve even higher performance with VERA. For example, GPT-6.1 Sol improves pulmonary nodule detection from 10.8% to 69.2% with VERA, demonstrating the complementary benefits of stronger model capabilities and an effective medical visual harness. Our results highlight the potential of visual harnesses as a new paradigm for scaling general VLMs to medical imaging tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 VERA 医疗视觉 harness，为通用 VLM 配备交互式视觉工具和无损诊断证据记忆，并通过遗漏与可靠性评估驱动迭代检查、测量和答案修订。
AI.relevance_reason: 工具化反复取证与证据记忆可对应「LOOK」与视觉证据筛选，遗漏评估触发的修订循环则可供核查「STOP」的停止依据与计算成本；但其证据走显式文本记忆而非 latent 状态，与 LVR 内部状态工作的联系需进一步判断。
